newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases after earlier demand for T-bill sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases after earlier demand for T-bill sales.

text.p: The rouble firmed in early trade before Wednesday's Treasury bill sales but then edged down after banks stopped actively seeking funds, dealers said on Tuesday.
"These are normal fluctuations. Rouble credits were more expensive in the morning ahead of the auctions, and banks preferred to sell dollars. The trend changed afterwards," one dealer said.
On Wednesday, the central bank will auction eight trillion roubles of new six-month paper and an additional tranche of three trillion roubles of six-month bills.

Another dealer said today settlement rates were also fluctuating as banks closed positions following three successive trading sessions each with Tuesday value dates because of the U.S. Veterans' Day holiday on Monday.
Russian banks use American counterparties for settlement.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,474-76 per dollar compared with an early 5,472-74. Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,478-80 per dollar from Monday's late 5,474-76.
The central bank said it had set 5,471/5,481 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 20-30 percent compared with an early 30-40 and Monday's late 5-10 percent.
